capacity.et: 2025. aastal oli Eestis kokku 61,1 tuh. majutuskohta ehk voodikohta, mis on 9,9x rohkem kui 1992. aastal. Sellele vaatamata jäi voodikohtade täituvus mõõdukaks: keskmine hõivatuse määr oli 35,0%, mis näitab, et suurem osa pakutavast mahutavusest jäi aasta jooksul kasutamata. Pikaajaline pakkumise kasv on selgelt ületanud nõudluse kasvu tempot, mistõttu majutusettevõtete voodikohad seisid keskmiselt kaks kolmandikku ajast tühjana. See annab tervikpildi Eesti majutussektori mahust ja selle kasutusastmest võrreldes taasiseseisvumisjärgse algperioodiga.
capacity.en: Estonia's accommodation stock reached 61.1 th beds in 2025, a 9.9x increase compared with 1992. Despite this large expansion in supply, the average bed occupancy rate stood at just 35.0% for the year, meaning most available beds sat unused across the period. The long-term growth in capacity has clearly outpaced demand growth, leaving accommodation providers with substantial spare capacity throughout 2025. Together these figures give a picture of both the scale of Estonia's accommodation sector and how intensively that capacity is actually being used compared to the early post-independence years.
capacity.highlightEt: 2025. aastal oli Eestis 61,1 tuh. voodikohta, kuid keskmine täituvus jäi vaid 35,0% juurde.
capacity.highlightEn: Estonia had 61.1 th beds in 2025, yet average occupancy reached only 35.0% of capacity.

dashboard.et: 2026. aasta juunis majutati Eestis kokku 395,3 tuh. külastajat, mis on 1,2% rohkem kui aasta varem samal kuul. Ööbimiste arv kasvas kiiremini, ulatudes 718,4 tuh. ööni ehk 1,9% võrra rohkem kui mullu, ning keskmine ööbimiste arv külastaja kohta tõusis 1,82-ni (+0,7%). Kuu jooksul oli välisturiste (221,6 tuh.) rohkem kui Eesti elanikest külastajaid (173,7 tuh.). Aasta algusest juunini kokku on Eestis majutatud juba 1,7 miljonit külastajat, mis on 4,1% enam kui samal perioodil eelmisel aastal — seega on 2026. aasta seni selgelt kasvutrendis. Kõige rohkem külastajaid võttis juunis vastu Harju maakond, 205,2 tuh. inimest ehk 2,8% rohkem kui aasta tagasi.
dashboard.en: In June 2026, Estonia recorded 395.3 th accommodated guests, up 1.2% year on year. Nights spent grew faster, reaching 718.4 th, a 1.9% increase, while the average length of stay rose to 1.82 nights per guest (+0.7%). Foreign visitors (221.6 th) outnumbered domestic guests (173.7 th) during the month. Cumulatively, from January through June 2026, Estonia has welcomed 1.7 million guests, 4.1% more than in the same period last year, pointing to solid growth so far this year. Harju county remained the most visited region in June, hosting 205.2 th guests, up 2.8% from a year earlier.

expenses.et: 2025. aastal kulutas Eesti elanik keskmiselt 163 eurot ühe siseriikliku reisi kohta, mis on 11,9% vähem kui aasta varem — selge langus reisikulutustes. Suurima kuluartikli moodustas majutus, millele kulus keskmiselt 49 eurot reisi kohta ehk ligi kolmandik kogukulust. See näitab, et majutus jääb siseturistide jaoks kõige suuremaks üksikuks väljaminekuks, samal ajal kui üldine reisile kuluv summa on aastaga märgatavalt kahanenud. Andmed pärinevad Statistikaameti tabelist TU552 ja kajastavad ainult Eesti elanike siseriiklikke reise.
expenses.en: In 2025, Estonians spent on average €163 per domestic trip, down 11.9% from the previous year, a notable drop in travel spending. Accommodation was the single largest expense category, averaging €49 per trip, close to a third of total spending. This confirms accommodation as the biggest individual cost driver for domestic travellers, even as overall trip spending fell sharply compared with the year before. The figures, drawn from Statistics Estonia's TU552 table, cover only domestic trips taken by Estonian residents.
expenses.highlightEt: 2025. aastal kahanes keskmine kulu siseriikliku reisi kohta 163 euroni, langedes aastaga 11,9%.
expenses.highlightEn: Average spending per domestic trip fell to €163 in 2025, down 11.9% year on year.

map.et: Viimase 24 kuu jooksul on kõige rohkem ööbimisi kogunenud Harju maakonda — kokku 7,4 miljonit ööd, mis kinnitab pealinnaregiooni selget liidripositsiooni Eesti majutusturul. Välisturistide seas on viimase 12 kuu jooksul suurimaks päritoluriigiks olnud Soome, kust pärines 671,0 tuh. külastajat. Värskeim kuu, 2026. aasta juuni, näitab jätkuvalt tasakaalus jaotust: 173,7 tuh. Eesti elanikku ja 221,6 tuh. välisturisti kasutasid Eesti majutusasutusi. See kinnitab, et nii kodumaine kui ka piiriülene nõudlus, eriti Soomest, kujundavad jätkuvalt Eesti majutusturu piirkondlikku ja hooajalist pilti.
map.en: Over the past 24 months, Harju county has drawn the most overnight stays nationally, totalling 7.4 million nights and underlining its dominance in Estonia's accommodation market. Among foreign visitors, Finland has been the leading country of origin over the last 12 months, contributing 671.0 th guests. The most recent month, June 2026, shows a similar pattern of mixed demand, with 173.7 th domestic guests alongside 221.6 th foreign visitors. Together these figures highlight how both local demand and cross-border travel, particularly from Finland, continue to shape Estonia's regional and seasonal tourism landscape.
map.highlightEt: Harju maakond juhib 7,4 milj. ööbimisega 24 kuu peale, Soome on suurim välisturistide allikas 671,0 tuh. külastajaga.
map.highlightEn: Harju county leads with 7.4 million nights over 24 months, while Finland remains the top source of foreign guests at 671.0 th.

purpose.et: Viimase 24 kuu andmed näitavad, et puhkusereisid domineerivad selgelt Eesti majutusstatistikas: need moodustasid 58% kõigist ööbimistest, jättes ärireisid ja muud eesmärgid selgesse vähemusse. Kestuse osas eelistavad reisijad lühikesi väljasõite — 2026. aasta esimeses kvartalis oli kõige levinum reisi pikkus 1 kuni 3 ööd, kokku 590,8 tuh. reisiga nii sise- kui ka välisreiside puhul kokku. See kinnitab, et Eesti majutusturgu kujundavad eelkõige lühikesed puhkusereisid, mitte pikemad või tööga seotud sõidud, mis mõjutab nii nõudluse hooajalisust kui ka majutuskohtade planeerimist.
purpose.en: Data from the last 24 months confirm that leisure travel dominates Estonia's accommodation sector, accounting for 58% of all nights spent, well ahead of business and other trip purposes. On duration, short getaways are clearly preferred: in the first quarter of 2026, trips lasting 1 to 3 nights were the most common, totalling 590.8 th trips across both domestic and foreign travel. Together, these figures show that Estonia's accommodation demand is shaped mainly by brief leisure stays rather than longer or work-related trips, a pattern relevant for both seasonal planning and capacity management.
purpose.highlightEt: Puhkusereisid moodustavad 58% ööbimistest, samal ajal kui lühireisid 1–3 ööd olid kõige levinumad — 590,8 tuh. reisi I kvartalis.
purpose.highlightEn: Leisure trips make up 58% of all nights, while 1-3 night stays were most common, with 590.8 th trips in Q1 2026.

EE00390000000000.en: Hiiu county had a mixed June 2026, with guest numbers falling 10.5% year-on-year to 4.2 th, yet nights spent actually rose 4.0% to 7.5 th, pointing to visitors staying longer despite fewer arrivals. Domestic travelers made up the bulk of guests at 3.5 th, compared to just 647 foreign visitors, reflecting the island's continued appeal mainly to Estonian tourists. Average nights per guest climbed notably by 16.3% to 1.80, reinforcing the longer-stay trend. The county represented a modest 1.1% share of Estonia's total guests this period. The year-to-date picture is more concerning, with cumulative guests for January–June down 17.9% compared to the same months last year, reaching only 8.7 th. This suggests that while June showed some resilience in terms of stay duration, the overall first half of 2026 has been considerably weaker for Hiiu than the prior year, warranting attention to what's driving the sustained drop in visitor numbers.

EE00450000000000.en: Ida-Viru county saw a softer June 2026, with 19.5 th guests accommodated, down 4.8% from a year earlier, and nights spent falling similarly by 4.0% to 37.2 th. Domestic guests continued to dominate the region's visitor base, with 16.0 th locals against just 3.5 th foreign travelers. Average nights per guest ticked up slightly by 0.8% to 1.91, suggesting stays held roughly steady even as arrivals declined. The county captured 4.9% of Estonia's total guests for the month. Despite the monthly dip, the year-to-date trend remains positive: cumulative guests for January–June 2026 reached 93.0 th, up 1.6% versus the same period last year. This indicates that earlier months in the year likely outperformed June, helping the region stay in growth territory overall even as the most recent month cooled. The strong domestic guest base continues to be the backbone of tourism activity in Ida-Viru.

EE00500000000000.en: Jõgeva county posted a positive June 2026, with guests accommodated rising 10.5% year-on-year to 2.3 th and nights spent up 4.9% to 3.4 th. Domestic visitors made up the vast majority at 2.1 th, compared to just 260 foreign guests, highlighting the county's reliance on local travelers. Average nights per guest, however, slipped 5.1% to 1.46, meaning visitors on average stayed slightly shorter even as their numbers grew. Jõgeva accounted for a modest 0.6% of Estonia's total guests this period. Looking at the full first half of the year, the picture is essentially flat, with cumulative guests for January–June reaching 7.1 th, down a slight 2.1% compared to the same months in 2025. This suggests June's rebound has helped offset softer earlier months, leaving the county roughly stable overall. With such a small foreign visitor base, Jõgeva's tourism performance remains closely tied to domestic travel patterns and preferences.

EE00520000000000.en: Järva county faced a difficult June 2026, with guests accommodated down 20.3% year-on-year to just 2.0 th, and nights spent falling 15.9% to 3.5 th. Domestic travelers accounted for the majority at 1.7 th guests, with only 322 foreign visitors recorded. On a brighter note, average nights per guest rose 5.5% to 1.70, indicating that those who did visit tended to stay a bit longer. The county's share of Estonia's total guests this period was just 0.5%, reflecting its small scale within the national tourism landscape. The year-to-date figures confirm a challenging first half of 2026, with cumulative guests reaching only 10.2 th, down a sharp 20.4% compared to the same period last year. This consistent decline across both the latest month and the cumulative period points to a broader slowdown in visitor interest in Järva that has persisted throughout the year rather than being a one-off monthly dip.

EE00560000000000.en: Lääne county continued to experience declining visitor numbers in June 2026, with guests accommodated down 9.3% year-on-year to 13.4 th and nights spent falling a similar 9.4% to 20.4 th. Domestic guests outnumbered foreign visitors, with 10.3 th locals against 3.1 th from abroad. Average nights per guest held nearly steady, dipping just 0.1% to 1.52, suggesting the drop was driven by fewer visitors rather than shorter stays. The county made up 3.4% of Estonia's total guests for the month. The broader year-to-date trend echoes this weakness, with cumulative guests for January–June 2026 totaling 45.7 th, down 10.6% from the same period a year earlier. This consistency between the monthly and cumulative figures indicates a sustained softening in demand across the first half of the year rather than a temporary dip, suggesting Lääne's tourism sector has faced headwinds throughout much of 2026 so far.

EE00600000000000.en: Lääne-Viru county recorded a decline in guests accommodated in June 2026, down 6.6% year-on-year to 12.9 th, though nights spent held nearly steady, dipping just 0.2% to 22.0 th. Domestic visitors led with 9.4 th guests, while foreign travelers numbered 3.5 th. Notably, average nights per guest rose 6.8% to 1.71, showing that despite fewer arrivals, those who came stayed considerably longer. The county represented 3.3% of Estonia's total guests this period. Cumulatively, the first half of 2026 has been fairly stable for Lääne-Viru, with guests for January–June reaching 50.1 th, down just 1.4% compared to the same months last year. This near-flat year-to-date performance suggests that June's weaker arrival numbers were largely offset by stronger results earlier in the year, and the rising average stay length may be helping cushion the overall visitor experience and revenue potential despite the dip in headcount.

EE00640000000000.en: Põlva county enjoyed a strong June 2026, with guests accommodated climbing 12.4% year-on-year to 2.5 th and nights spent surging 19.4% to 3.8 th, one of the more notable growth stories among smaller counties this period. Domestic visitors dominated at 2.3 th guests, compared to just 181 from abroad. Average nights per guest also rose, up 6.2% to 1.50, indicating visitors were both more numerous and staying somewhat longer. Põlva's share of Estonia's total guests remained modest at 0.6%. This monthly strength is reflected in the year-to-date numbers too, with cumulative guests for January–June 2026 reaching 8.2 th, up 2.2% versus the same period last year. The alignment between a strong June and a positive cumulative trend suggests Põlva's tourism sector has been building momentum through the first half of the year, with growth in both visitor numbers and length of stay pointing to healthy underlying demand.

EE00680000000000.en: Pärnu county posted solid growth in June 2026, with 51.0 th guests accommodated, up 3.4% year-on-year, alongside a smaller 0.7% rise in nights spent to 93.9 th. The visitor base was nearly evenly split between 26.2 th domestic and 24.8 th foreign guests, reflecting the county's broad appeal. Average nights per guest fell 2.6% to 1.84, suggesting that while more people visited, they trimmed their stays slightly. Pärnu county captured a substantial 12.9% share of Estonia's total guests this period, ranking among the country's leading destinations. The year-to-date trend reinforces this positive momentum, with cumulative guests for January–June 2026 reaching 202.3 th, up 2.7% compared to the same months last year. This consistent growth across both the latest month and the cumulative period points to steady demand throughout the first half of 2026, with the county's balanced mix of domestic and international visitors supporting resilient overall performance.

EE00710000000000.en: Rapla county saw guest numbers rise 15.9% year-on-year in June 2026 to 2.1 th, yet nights spent plunged 47.1% to just 4.0 th, a striking divergence pointing to much shorter average stays. Domestic guests made up most of the visitor base at 1.9 th, with 283 foreign travelers. Indeed, average nights per guest collapsed 54.4% to 1.89, the sharpest such drop among the counties this period, meaning visitors are arriving in greater numbers but leaving much sooner than before. Rapla accounted for just 0.5% of Estonia's total guests this month. Over the first half of 2026, cumulative guests reached 6.4 th, up a modest 1.0% versus the same period last year, showing that despite June's unusual stay-length shift, the county's overall visitor volume has held roughly steady. This suggests a changing pattern of shorter, more frequent visits rather than an outright decline in interest in Rapla.

EE00740000000000.en: Saare county experienced a softer June 2026, with guests accommodated down 3.3% year-on-year to 22.3 th and nights spent falling 4.0% to 37.2 th. The visitor mix leaned domestic, with 13.8 th local guests compared to 8.6 th from abroad, though foreign visitors still made up a meaningful share. Average nights per guest slipped slightly, down 0.8% to 1.67, indicating stays shortened only marginally alongside the drop in arrivals. Saare's share of Estonia's total guests this period stood at 5.6%. Despite the monthly softness, the year-to-date outlook remains positive, with cumulative guests for January–June 2026 reaching 67.6 th, up 1.9% compared to the same months last year. This suggests earlier months in the year outperformed June, allowing the island county to maintain overall growth for the first half of 2026 even as the latest month showed some cooling in visitor demand.

EE00790000000000.en: Tartu county delivered steady growth in June 2026, with guests accommodated up 3.1% year-on-year to 30.0 th, while nights spent edged up just 0.2% to 49.3 th. The visitor base was fairly balanced, with 15.5 th foreign guests slightly outnumbering 14.6 th domestic travelers, highlighting the county's international draw. Average nights per guest fell 2.8% to 1.64, suggesting shorter average stays even as overall visitor numbers grew. Tartu county captured a solid 7.6% share of Estonia's total guests this period. The year-to-date trajectory looks even stronger, with cumulative guests for January–June 2026 reaching 141.8 th, up 4.9% compared to the same period last year. This consistent growth across both the latest month and the cumulative figures points to sustained momentum in the county's tourism sector, with the near-even split between domestic and foreign visitors reflecting broad-based appeal to both markets throughout the first half of the year.

EE00810000000000.en: Valga county posted modest growth in June 2026, with guests accommodated up 0.9% year-on-year to 13.0 th and nights spent rising 2.0% to 25.8 th. Domestic visitors dominated the mix at 11.1 th guests, far outnumbering the 1.9 th foreign travelers. Average nights per guest rose slightly, up 1.1% to 1.98, among the longest average stays recorded across the counties this period. Valga accounted for 3.3% of Estonia's total guests this month. The standout figure, however, is the year-to-date performance: cumulative guests for January–June 2026 reached 63.6 th, up an impressive 12.8% compared to the same period last year, one of the strongest cumulative gains among all counties. This suggests that while June itself brought only modest gains, earlier months in 2026 saw substantially stronger growth, giving Valga a very healthy overall trajectory for the first half of the year despite the more moderate latest monthly result.

EE00840000000000.en: Viljandi county had a positive June 2026, with guests accommodated rising 7.2% year-on-year to 6.6 th and nights spent up a similar 7.1% to 10.4 th. Domestic guests led the visitor mix with 5.5 th, compared to 1.1 th foreign travelers. Average nights per guest stayed essentially flat, down just 0.1% to 1.58, indicating the growth came from more visitors rather than longer stays. Viljandi's share of Estonia's total guests this period was 1.7%. This monthly strength carries through to the cumulative figures as well, with guests for January–June 2026 reaching 21.8 th, up 5.5% compared to the same months last year. The alignment between solid June growth and a healthy year-to-date increase suggests Viljandi has enjoyed consistent, broad-based momentum in its tourism sector throughout the first half of 2026, with domestic travelers continuing to form the backbone of the county's visitor base.

EE00870000000000.en: Võru county saw steady, modest growth in June 2026, with guests accommodated up 2.0% year-on-year to 8.1 th and nights spent rising more notably by 6.1% to 15.1 th. Domestic visitors made up the bulk of guests at 6.9 th, compared to 1.2 th foreign travelers. Average nights per guest increased 4.1% to 1.85, suggesting visitors stayed somewhat longer even as arrival growth was moderate. Võru's share of Estonia's total guests this period stood at 2.1%. The year-to-date trend is similarly positive, with cumulative guests for January–June 2026 reaching 33.5 th, up 1.8% compared to the same period last year. This consistency between the latest month and the cumulative figures points to steady, if unspectacular, growth in Võru's tourism sector throughout the first half of 2026, with the rising average length of stay a particularly encouraging sign for the county's accommodation providers.

EE00370784000004.en: Tallinn remained Estonia's tourism heavyweight in June 2026, drawing 189.7 th guests, up 3.4% year-on-year, who logged 356.2 th nights spent, a robust 6.0% increase. Foreign visitors overwhelmingly dominated the mix at 151.2 th against just 38.4 th domestic guests, underscoring the capital's role as the country's main international gateway. Average nights per guest rose 2.5% to 1.88, showing visitors are both more numerous and staying a bit longer. The city alone accounted for a remarkable 48.0% of all guests recorded nationwide this period. The year-to-date picture is equally strong, with cumulative guests for January–June 2026 reaching 844.8 th, up 6.6% compared to the same months last year, one of the strongest cumulative gains among all regions. This combination of solid monthly growth and even stronger year-to-date momentum confirms Tallinn's continued dominance of Estonian tourism, driven overwhelmingly by international visitor demand throughout the first half of 2026.

EE00680624661905.en: Pärnu city saw modest growth in June 2026, with guests accommodated up 0.9% year-on-year to 39.4 th, even as nights spent slipped 1.6% to 76.9 th, pointing to slightly shorter average visits. Foreign guests edged out domestic ones, with 23.0 th visitors from abroad compared to 16.4 th locals. Average nights per guest fell 2.4% to 1.95, still among the longer average stays recorded across Estonian regions. The city captured a notable 10.0% share of Estonia's total guests this period. Looking at the full first half of the year, cumulative guests for January–June 2026 reached 182.3 th, up 1.7% compared to the same months last year. This steady, if modest, year-to-date growth suggests Pärnu city has maintained a fairly consistent tourism performance through 2026 so far, with its strong foreign visitor base and comparatively long average stays continuing to define the seaside city's appeal despite the slight softening in nights spent this month.

EE00790793815105.en: Tartu city posted solid growth in June 2026, with guests accommodated up 3.4% year-on-year to 26.9 th, while nights spent rose more modestly by 1.4% to 44.6 th. Foreign visitors slightly outnumbered domestic ones, at 15.0 th against 11.9 th, highlighting the city's strong international appeal. Average nights per guest fell 2.0% to 1.66, suggesting stays shortened a touch even as visitor numbers grew. Tartu city accounted for 6.8% share of Estonia's total guests this period, a significant contribution among Estonia's urban destinations. The year-to-date trend mirrors this strength, with cumulative guests for January–June 2026 reaching 132.9 th, up 4.9% compared to the same period last year. This consistency between the latest month's growth and the cumulative year-to-date figure points to sustained momentum in Tartu city's tourism sector throughout the first half of 2026, with international visitors playing an increasingly central role in the city's accommodation demand.
